label: start
name: starting architecture
last_analysis: All 9 trials scored exactly 0 on both seeds, and training success was also 0. The trials covered more samples, more exploration, a DONE prior, deeper nets, dense and MLP heads, and flip or transpose heads, so no single idea has shown a signal. One factor has gone unnoticed: every recipe so far cut the number of gradient steps. The default makes 32 updates × 4 epochs × 32 minibatches = 4,096 steps; r1c1 made about 1,900 and r1c3 about 1,660. Getting an exact build depends on precise per-anchor decisions about where each brick lands, which may need many small, low-noise updates rather than more fresh samples. In this final round I test (a) the baseline with about 2× the gradient steps on 64-sample minibatches; (b) a head whose learned convolution has the brick's own footprint as its kernel, so it sees each covered cell individually, plus that recipe; (c) global self-attention so every cell sees the whole design, to help with ordering and with choosing DONE.
